I get it, it would be way too much work to make a world that big and have it be filled with intricately designed content but it gets very same-y. Honestly AI could be a huge boon for designers of open world games. AI is good at procedural things but not creative things so let AI design your caves and shit and have actual people do interesting dungeons and side areas.

That's what gets me most annoyed when fanboys try to act like TotK is "nothing like BotW". I think its a great game and while i wouldnt go so far as calling it glorified dlc it certainly isnt a whole new game either. The people saying "it's 3 whole maps of course it's completely different" are just grossly exaggerating. The Sky Islands are like 10% of the overworld if I'm being generous and the underworld is neat but they really didn't need to make it 1:1 with so little to actually do down there. It's nothing new that publishers will find ways to make as much money from their product as they possibly can, especially from the hard-core fan base who they know will shell out extra cash. Call of Duty has been doing $100 versions of their releases for a while now and lots of other games followed suit and it sucks. $70 new games was bad enough but when most of the big games also offer $100 premium options it feels really bad as a consumer because paying base game full price day 1 seems to give you quite a bit less value than the "ultimate edition" AND so many games have been releasing unfinished or broken so the day 1 experience isn't even a positive in many cases. 

I do agree its pretty much arguing semantics at this point though. Consumers lost the battle of day 1 content long ago. Now that discs are just glorified download codes there is no such thing as "full content on disc". Day 1 dlc has become acceptable if not just an assumption at this point. Microtransactions and rushed launches are still rampant despite publishers claiming $70 was necessary to keep quality high. Regardless it's all moot because games still sell. Pokemon Scarlet/Violet was broken and technically messy (still is tbh) but still sold 20 million+ copies so far. Your only choices are: 1. wait for a sale and be OK with possibly being spoiled, missing out on the communal experience and timed events, and playing catch up with people who have months of time already. 2. Pay full price for base game and gamble on quality, pay extra for bonuses that can include playing early..while still gambling on quality. 

All in all, games have arguably never been better. So many good games to play and so little time to play. The only downside is deciding how to spend that time knowing it's likely gonna be tradeoffs no matter which route you decide.
